text:
simon: Quick perf note — GQA vs MQA kernel picks are causing weird regressions on Hopper pools. Repro and numbers below. Anyone seen layout sensitivity with KV page sizes?

anya: yep, saw a similar blip last week with quantized 7B. It looked layout-dependent (interleaved vs contiguous KV). Can you drop the profiler output?

simon: Paste from local H100 run:
```
Model: instr-7b-q, device: H100-80GB (driver 535)
Workload: mixed short (32) and long (512) sequences, batching=auto
Seq 32 (batch=32): throughput=5200 tok/s, p50=18ms, p95=42ms
Seq 512 (batch=8): throughput=780 tok/s, p50=120ms, p95=260ms
Kernel breakdown (seq512 heavy):
 - kv_cache_load_interleaved_bs64 : 25% time (44us/op)
 - paged_attn_bs32_dense         : 40% time (70us/op)
 - gqa_matmul_8x32              : 10% time
 - softmax/other                : 25%
Notes: forcing a bs128 paged kernel reduces kv_load time (~-30%) but increases attn kernel memory traffic and stalls, net +2% latency for seq32 but -18% for seq512.
```

benchbot: perf-run 2025-10-31T09:12Z results: seq512 median latency +12% on H100 vs baseline (Ampere) when using current autotuner picks. Regression isolated to paged_attn kernel selection.

kkim: My guess: autotuner cost model uses compute FLOPs + simplistic mem estimate; it ignores per-layer KV stride and block alignment. On H100 the best kernel depends on whether KV pages align to 128B lanes — misalignment kills coalescing.

mike: Agreed. Two main factors we missed: 1) MQA group count changes access pattern (grouped heads lead to non-unit stride), 2) per-layer kv_cache layout (interleaved vs contiguous) affects whether a paged variant wins.

simon: Proposed quick plan:
 - add per-device microbench at startup to measure paged_attn and kv_load variants over block sizes (32/64/128)
 - extend autotuner to include a layout-aware penalty term (kv_stride % 128 != 0 -> +X latency)
 - prefer MQA-specialized kernels when groups>1 for seq_len>128
 - log autotuner decision and microbench ids in traces for postmortem

anya: +1. Also add safe rollout: canary 5% traffic + p95 guardrails (reject if +8% vs baseline). We should avoid flipping everyone's production kernels mid-deploy. :no_entry_sign:

kkim: Microbench CLI prototype:
```
# run quick per-device kernel sweep, outputs CSV
runtune --device h100 --test paged_attn --block-sizes 32,64,128 --iters 50 --out /tmp/h100_paged_results.csv
# CSV columns: kernel,block_size,median_us,stdev_us
```

mike: For autotuner cost model, suggestion: cost = FLOPs/compute_perf + mem_bytes/peak_mem_bw + misalign_penalty*(kv_stride % align_factor != 0) . Microbench will give us realistic compute_perf and mem_bandwidth numbers per kernel variant.

simon: I'll prototype the autotune patch (add prefer_block_size + preflight_microbench options) and a sparse logging field `autotune_choice` in traces. Plan to open PR today.

benchbot: note: bench harness will run a A/B with both kernel sets once PR lands. Expect 4-6h run for 3 devices.

anya: owners: simon -> autotune logic + trace logging, kkim -> microbench harness + CSV ingestion, mike -> cost model and rollout policy. I'll own the canary SLA checks in console.

simon: ack. I'll include a small test: reproduce the earlier regression locally with `--force-kernel paged_attn_bs32_dense` and then show improvement with new pick.

kkim: one more: consider exposing an emergency override flag `RW_DISABLE_PAGED_KERNELS=true` for customer-facing nodes in case of unexpected regressions.

mike: yes, feature flag + automatic fallback to baseline kernel if p95 exceeds threshold during rollout.

simon: thanks team — will post PR link and perf diffs here when ready. cc @eng-runtime

anya: :thumbsup:
